newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan computer firm debuts in new stock market.
newsitem.headline: Japan computer firm debuts in new stock market.

text.p: A small Japanese computer software maker successfully went public on Tuesday, the first company to do so under a new scheme that helps loss-making but promising ventures raise funds from the equities market.

ATL Systems Inc drew an initial offer price of 319,000 yen ($2,823), up 39,000 yen ($345) from the public offer price, on the new second section of Japan's over-the-counter (OTC) market. It climbed to 424,000 yen ($3,752) in late trading.
Based in Yamanashi prefecture in eastern Japan, ATL's mainstay product is a sales and management package software.
"We drew lots of attention," ATL president Naruo Naito told Reuters.

The Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA), which set up the second section of the OTC market to make it easier for venture companies to raise funds, said a second small venture, A&Cmos Inc, a Tokyo-based integrated circuit developer and maker, will register on the second section through a public offering on December 25.

The section is designed to help venture businesses, especially research-oriented and high-tech ones, go public through simpler registration procedures and requirements, even if they are losing money, the JSDA said.

Before the formation of the market, such high-risk ventures had problems issuing shares due to a lack of steady profits and recent studies show that an increasing number of venture companies are keen to go public.
ATL said on Tuesday that it had posted a parent current loss of 32 million yen ($283,000) in the six months to October 31, against a loss of 13 million yen ($115,000) in the same period a year ago.
Current profit is pre-tax profit and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
The company said it would post a parent current profit of 84 million yen ($743,000) in the year to April 30, against a loss of 26 million yen ($230,000) in the year-ago period. ($1=113 yen)
